previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of heart surgery was admitted after presenting with diabetic ketoacidosis and elevated cardiac enzymes indicating a non-ST elevation myocardial infarction. She had no chest pain but was found to have new severe left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction of 19%. A stress test revealed fixed perfusion defects, and cardiac catheterization showed significant coronary artery disease, leading to stent placement in multiple vessels. She was treated for DKA with insulin, managed for acute systolic heart failure with dialysis, and started on dual antiplatelet therapy. A small, asymptomatic arteriovenous fistula was incidentally found and deemed non-interventional. Cellulitis of the right index finger was treated with IV antibiotics, transitioning to oral doxycycline. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Ms. ___,

You were admitted to ___ and 
underwent a fistula ligation, HD catheter placement and 
dialysis. You are recovering well and are now ready for 
discharge. Please follow the instructions below to continue your 
recovery:

Please call your doctor or nurse practitioner or return to the 
Emergency Department for any of the following:
*You experience new chest pain, pressure, squeezing or 
tightness.
*New or worsening cough, shortness of breath, or wheeze.
*If you are vomiting and cannot keep down fluids or your 
medications.
*You are getting dehydrated due to continued vomiting, diarrhea, 
or other reasons. Signs of dehydration include dry mouth, rapid 
heartbeat, or feeling dizzy or faint when standing.
*You see blood or dark/black material when you vomit or have a 
bowel movement.
*You experience burning when you urinate, have blood in your 
urine, or experience a discharge.
*Your pain in not improving within ___ hours or is not gone 
within 24 hours. Call or return immediately if your pain is 
getting worse or changes location or moving to your chest or 
back.
*You have shaking chills, or fever greater than 101.5 degrees 
Fahrenheit or 38 degrees Celsius.
*Any change in your symptoms, or any new symptoms that concern 
you.

Please resume all regular home medications, unless specifically 
advised not to take a particular medication. Also, please take 
any new medications as prescribed.

Please get plenty of rest, continue to ambulate several times 
per day, and drink adequate amounts of fluids. Avoid lifting 
weights greater than ___ lbs until you follow-up with your 
surgeon.
Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery while taking pain 
medications.

increased pain, swelling, redness, or drainage from the incision 
site.

and warm water. Gently pat the area dry.

appointment.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CTA UPPER EXTREMITY

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with PAD, chronic b/l hand ischemia  // r/o
vascular inflow lesion. please do runoff b/l upper extremities

TECHNIQUE:  ___ MDCT images were obtained through the upper extremities before,
then after the administration of IV contrast in the arterial and delayed
phases.  Multiplanar reformatted images in coronal and sagittal axis were
generated and reviewed.

COMPARISON:  None.

DOSE:  Total DLP (Body) = 1,019 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS: 

LEFT:  The left subclavian, axillary, and brachial arteries appear to be well
opacified, without evidence of an occlusive embolus.  The left radial and
ulnar arteries are extremely calcified, and given the resolution of CT,
presence of flow cannot be assessed through these arteries, as well as the
arteries of the hand.  Incidental note is made of a left arteriovenous
fistula, which does not demonstrate any flow.

RIGHT:  The right subclavian, axillary, and brachial arteries also appear to
be well opacified, without evidence of an occlusive embolus, although
evaluation of the origin of the right subclavian artery is limited due to
overlying streak artifact.  The right radial and ulnar arteries are extremely
calcified, and again given the resolution of CT, presents flow cannot be
assessed through these arteries, or the arteries of the hand.

CTA CHEST:  The main, lobar, segmental, and subsegmental pulmonary arteries
appear to be well opacified without evidence of a filling defect, concerning
for a pulmonary embolus.

The thyroid is normal.  There is no axillary, hilar, or mediastinal
lymphadenopathy.  The heart size is mildly enlarged.  Note is made of an
artificial mitral valve.  The esophagus is normal without evidence of a hiatal
hernia.

The airways are patent to the subsegmental levels.  No pulmonary nodules
concerning for malignancy identified.  There is no pleural effusion, or
pneumothorax.

The study is not tailored for evaluation of the subdiaphragmatic structures,
however incidental note is made of a 1.4 cm cystic lesion in the pancreatic
head, adjacent to the common bile duct and likely secondary to an IPMN.  There
is evidence of cholelithiasis, without evidence of cholecystitis.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  No lytic or blastic lesions concerning for malignancy are
identified.  Old right-sided rib fractures are identified in the right ___,
___, and 5th ribs.  Central wedging is seen involving the T6, T8, and T9
vertebral bodies, of indeterminate chronicity.


IMPRESSION: 

1.  Arteries in the upper extremities bilaterally appear to be well opacified
through the brachials to the level of the elbow.  Evaluation of the forearm
and wrist is limited, given the heavily calcified vessels.  Presence of flow
cannot be evaluated on this study.  An MRA or Upper extremity angiogram is
recommended for further evaluation of flow.

2.  No evidence of a pulmonary embolus.  No intrathoracic abnormalities
identified.

3.  1.4 cm cystic lesion in the head of the pancreas, statistically most
likely secondary to an IPMN, however can be further evaluated by MRI.

4.  Cholelithiasis.

5.  Occluded left forearm AV fistula.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Upper extremity angiogram or MRA is recommended to
evaluate for flow in the forearms and hands bilaterally.

MRI of the abdomen for evaluation of the cystic pancreatic lesion

NOTIFICATION:  ___ were d/w Dr. ___ at 6pm on the day of the exam by
phone by Dr. ___.

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with ESRD // please place tunneled HD line

COMPARISON:  CTA ___.

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___ and Dr.
___ radiologist performed the procedure. Dr. ___
supervised the trainee during the key components of the procedure and has
reviewed and agrees with the trainee's findings.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
50 mcg of fentanyl and 0.5 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 21 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: 50 mcg fentanyl, 0.5 mg versed
CONTRAST: 0 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 1.9 min, 12 mGy

PROCEDURE:  PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the explanation of the risks,
benefits and alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was
obtained from the patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography
suite and placed supine on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was
performed per ___ protocol. The left upper chest was prepped and draped in
the usual sterile fashion.
Under continuous ultrasound guidance, the patent left internal jugular vein
was compressible and accessed using a micropuncture needle. Permanent
ultrasound images were obtained before and after intravenous access, which
confirmed vein patency. Subsequently a Nitinol wire was passed into the right
atrium using fluoroscopic guidance. The needle was exchanged for a
micropuncture sheath. The Nitinol wire was removed and a short ___ wire was
advanced to make appropriate measurements for catheter length. The ___ wire
was then passed distally into the IVC.
Next, attention was turned towards creation of a tunnel over the upper
anterior chest wall. After instilling superficial and deeper local anesthesia
using lidocaine mixed with epinephrine, a small skin incision was made at the
tunnel entry site. A 23cm tip-to-cuff length catheter was selected. The
catheter was tunneled from the entry site towards the venotomy site from where
it was brought out using a tunneling device. The venotomy tract was dilated
using the introducer of the peel-away sheath supplied. Following this, the
peel-away sheath was placed over the ___ wire through which the catheter was
threaded into the right side of the heart with the tip in the right atrium.
The sheath was then peeled away. The catheter was sutured in place with 0 silk
sutures. Steri-strips were also used to close the venotomy incision site.
Final spot fluoroscopic image demonstrating good alignment of the catheter and
no kinking. The tip is in the right atrium. The catheter was flushed and both
lumens were capped. Sterile dressings were applied. The patient tolerated the
procedure well.

FINDINGS: 

Patent left internal jugular vein.  Final fluoroscopic image showing
hemodialysis catheter with tip terminating in the right atrium.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful placement of a 23cm tip-to-cuff length tunneled dialysis line. The
tip of the catheter terminates in the right atrium. The catheter is ready for
use.
